{"id":"mimid-1wgh.78","title":"Live stream: frame and request size limits, 16 outstanding requests (INVENTED)","description":"Epic mimid-e64f; docs/design/binary-live-stream.md §5.4, §5.8.

Chosen by the agent for mimid-e64f, unattended (INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC):
- maxMessageBytes = 16 MiB + 64 KiB: no frame in either direction is larger; fits an Upload or FetchAsset answer of the largest blob mimid stores (MAX_BLOB_LEN, 16 MiB).
- maxRequestBytes = 4 MiB + 64 KiB: no client request other than Upload is larger; fits the largest MLS object mimid takes on any other route (MAX_BODY_LEN, 4 MiB), as JMAP maxSizeRequest does after base64url.
- A frame over either: Error tooLarge without id, connection closed. A text frame closes the connection.
- At most 16 outstanding requests per connection; one more is answered rateLimited.
Both limits are stated in ProviderHello.

new_value: {"notes":"Updated 2026-11-20 for findings log F10 (Mark: take; mimid-server advertises 4 MiB, both bindings use one limit; commit 48f5e33 on findings-impl): maxMlsObjectSize = 4 MiB (raw octets) in the mimi capability and in ProviderHello; the core functions refuse a larger MLS argument on both bindings (invalidArguments; KeyPackage/set SetError tooLarge). maxRequestBytes is now 2 x 4 MiB + 64 KiB and JMAP maxSizeRequest 2 x base64(4 MiB) + 64 KiB, so a Room/create with two max-size objects fits and the per-object limit is the one a client meets. Open: the protocol relay's MAX_BODY_LEN (4 MiB) caps the wrapped request, so an object within its envelope's size of 4 MiB is still refused there."}
